title_en: Dazhu County Rural Credit Cooperative Union v. Xizang Huaxi Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over a guarantee contract
ruling_gist_en: Paragraph 1 of Article 39 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China provides: 'Where the parties to the principal contract agree to use a new loan to repay an old loan, the surety shall not bear civil liability unless the surety knew or should have known about it.' Whether the circumstance falls under 'the surety knew or should have known' shall be determined based on a comprehensive analysis of the case. If the surety has an affiliated relationship with the borrower, undertakes in the suretyship contract to assume joint and several liability for the borrower's breach of contract such as diverting the use of the loan, and has actually performed part of the principal obligation, it may be determined that the surety knew or should have known that the principal obligation was to use a new loan to repay an old loan. Under such circumstances, if the surety claims to be exempted from civil liability on the ground of the above provision, the people's court shall not support it.

full_text_en:
Dazhu County Rural Credit Cooperative Union v. Tibet Huaxi Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over guarantee contract

[Ruling Summary]

Paragraph 1 of Article 39 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where the parties to the principal contract agree to use a new loan to repay an old loan, the guarantor shall not bear civil liability unless the guarantor knew or should have known of such arrangement." Whether a situation falls within the scope of "the guarantor knew or should have known" shall be determined based on a comprehensive analysis of the case facts. Where the guarantor has an affiliated relationship with the borrower, undertakes in the guarantee contract to assume joint and several liability for the borrower's acts in breach of contract such as diverting the use of the loan, and has actually performed part of the principal obligation, it may be determined that the guarantor knew or should have known that the principal obligation was a new loan used to repay an old loan. Under such circumstances, if the guarantor asserts that it should not bear civil liability on the ground of the above provision, the people's court shall not support such assertion.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2011) Min Shen Zi No. 429

Applicant for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Tibet Huaxi Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 93 Beijing Middle Road, Lhasa, Tibet Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Chen Dabin, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Lu Ming, Employee of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Xiong Bangguo, Lawyer of Sichuan Weihua Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Dazhu County Rural Credit Cooperative Union. Domicile: North Zhuyang Road, Zhuyang Town, Dazhu County, Sichuan Province.

Legal Representative: Zhou Dahua, Chairperson of the Credit Cooperative Union.

Agent ad litem: Cun Hui, Lawyer of Sichuan Times Jingwei Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Wentian, Lawyer of Sichuan Times Jingwei Law Firm.

The applicant for retrial, Tibet Huaxi Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huaxi Pharmaceutical), due to a dispute over a guarantee contract with the respondent, Dazhu County Rural Credit Cooperative Union (hereinafter referred to as Dazhu Credit Union), disagrees with the civil judgment (2010) Chuan Min Zhong Zi No. 131 rendered by the Sichuan High People's Court, and hereby applies to this Court for a retrial. This Court formed a collegiate panel in accordance with the law to examine this case, and the examination has now been concluded.

Huaxi Pharmaceutical applies for retrial on the following grounds: First, the first-instance and second-instance judgments have serious procedural violations, omit the main parties to this case, have an obvious intention to illegally collect and use evidence, fail to cross-examine the main evidence for determining the facts of the case, and have errors in the application of law, which conforms to the provisions of Article 179, Paragraph 1, Items (2) and (6), and Paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and therefore a retrial should be granted. Requests: 1. Revoke the civil judgment (2010) Chuan Min Zhong Zi No. 131 of the Sichuan High People's Court; 2. Dismiss the claims of Dazhu Credit Union; 3. Dazhu Credit Union shall bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances. The reasons are as follows: 1. The second-instance court violated legal procedures. (1) Although the borrower, Dachuan Area Fukang Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Fukang Company), had its business license revoked on April 16, 2001, it could still engage in litigation activities before being cancelled, and should have been added as a party. (2) The second-instance judgment violated legal procedures by admitting evidence whose authenticity could not be proven and evidence provided by Dazhu Credit Union in violation of legal procedures, and by using the testimony of witnesses who did not appear in court to be examined as the main evidence for determining the facts of the case. (3) The members of the collegiate panel stated in the notice of acceptance of the second-instance case were inconsistent with those stated in the judgment; the collegiate panel member Chen Hong stated in the judgment did not appear in court; and the second-instance court never informed Huaxi Pharmaceutical of the change in the collegiate panel members. 2. The second-instance judgment made erroneous findings of fact. Dazhu Credit Union knew that Fukang Company had changed the use of the loan, proving that they colluded with each other; Fukang Company and Dazhu Credit Union fabricated false loan procedures to defraud Huaxi Pharmaceutical into providing a guarantee. Fukang Company was an enterprise established by the Dazhou Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, and was under the same supervising bank as Dazhu Credit Union, thus having a conflict of interest. Dazhu Credit Union could not provide the necessary materials to prove the existence of a loan relationship between it and Fukang Company, Dachuan Area Yuanchang Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yuanchang Industry), and Dachuan Area Agricultural Resources Development Company (hereinafter referred to as Agricultural Resources Company), and it was impossible to use the loan of RMB 12 million to repay the overdue loans. The evidence submitted by Dazhu Credit Union could not prove that the loan of RMB 12 million had been actually disbursed. 3. Even if Dazhu Credit Union had disbursed the loan, it should be determined as a loan used to repay another loan. (1) From the analysis of the fund flow records, this case involves a virtual loan used to repay the old loan; Dazhu Credit Union knew that Fukang Company did not purchase raw materials as agreed and assisted in changing the use of the loan. (2) The second-instance court used evidence that had not been cross-examined and evidence that could not be used as the basis for determining the facts of the case to determine that Fukang Company had not changed the use of the loan. The Dazhou Jinzheng Judicial Appraisal Center's Da Jin Si Jian Zhong Xin (2009) Si Jian Zi No. 002 "Judicial Opinion Letter" was commissioned by Dazhu Credit Union unilaterally, and its conclusions were inconsistent with the facts found in this case, thus insufficient to serve as the basis for determining the facts. Among the four pieces of evidence obtained by the court ex officio, the "Consultation Record" and the "Investigation Record" constituted witness testimony; it was illegal to admit such evidence when the witnesses did not appear in court to testify, and the content of the evidence itself was contradictory. As the borrower, Fukang Company should have participated in the litigation, and because it had a conflict of interest with Dazhu Credit Union, the testimony of the legal representative of Fukang Company was not admissible as evidence. The two sets of vouchers for Dazhu Credit Union's loans to other companies and the "Report on the Proposed Transfer of Hainan Tongyuan Industrial General Company and Sichuan Dachuan Area Fukang Industrial Co., Ltd. to Chengdu Dayi Industry (Group) Co., Ltd." were not related to this case and could not be used as evidence. 4. The second-instance court determined that Huaxi Pharmaceutical should bear the guarantee liability without ascertaining whether Fukang Company had used the new loan to repay the old loan, which was erroneous. First, the legal representative of Huaxi Pharmaceutical learned during the litigation that the guarantee liability was a scam set up by Fukang Company and Dazhu Credit Union, and could not have known about the fact of using the new loan to repay the old loan. Second, the signature of Chen Dabin in the industrial and commercial registration materials of Fukang Company was forged, and Chen Dabin was not a shareholder or supervisor of Fukang Company. Third, the "Enterprise Merger Agreement" was a copy, and the parties denied its authenticity, so it could not be used as evidence. Therefore, the evidence of Dazhu Credit Union was insufficient to prove that Huaxi Pharmaceutical knew about the fact of using the new loan to repay the old loan.

Dazhu Credit Union submitted a written opinion stating: 1. The procedures in this case were lawful. (1) The parties to the litigation were properly constituted. The "Guaranteed Loan Contract" clearly stipulated that Huaxi Pharmaceutical voluntarily served as the guarantor for the borrower's timely repayment of the principal and interest of the loan under the contract, and assumed joint and several liability for the borrower's acts in breach of contract such as diverting the use of the loan. Dazhu Credit Union's claim against Huaxi Pharmaceutical was in accordance with the law and did not omit any main party. (2) All evidence submitted by Dazhu Credit Union was presented in original form and had been cross-examined in court; Huaxi Pharmaceutical confirmed this in multiple court sessions, as evidenced by the court records. (3) Although the witnesses who provided the written witness testimony submitted by Dazhu Credit Union and obtained by the court did not appear in court for cross-examination, according to Article 69 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, witness testimony from witnesses who did not appear in court can still serve as the basis for determining the facts of the case. (4) The second-instance court informed the parties of the change in the collegiate panel members during the court session, and both parties had no objection. 2. There was no collusion between Dazhu Credit Union and Fukang Company to defraud Huaxi Pharmaceutical into providing a guarantee; Huaxi Pharmaceutical knew the actual use of the loan. (1) Huaxi Pharmaceutical and its legal representative, Chen Dabin, actually controlled the loan. Huaxi Pharmaceutical affixed its seal to the "Loan Application" and the "Guaranteed Loan Contract", and its legal representative, Chen Dabin, personally signed; the industrial and commercial registration files of Fukang Company recorded Chen Dabin's shareholder status. In the original first and second instances before the case was remanded for retrial, Huaxi Pharmaceutical did not object to the authenticity, objectivity, or relevance of the industrial and commercial registration materials of Fukang Company, which constituted a self-admission. Shen Mingcheng, the legal representative of Fukang Company, confirmed that Chen Dabin was indeed the actual main operator of Fukang Company. Fukang Company's supervising authority was the Dazhou Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, and it was affiliated with Hainan Tongyuan Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hainan Company). Article 3 of the "Enterprise Merger Agreement" confirmed that the loan of RMB 51.19 million borrowed by Fukang Company from the Agricultural Bank was all invested in Hainan Company. The industrial and commercial registration materials of Hainan Company confirmed that its legal representative was Chen Dabin. The relevant evidence corroborated each other, showing that the actual responsible person of Fukang Company was Chen Dabin. At the same time, the Da Shi Nong Hang Fa (2000) No. 306 document obtained ex officio by the second-instance court confirmed that Chen Dabin was a shareholder of Fukang Company. The "Enterprise Merger Agreement" and its attached documents all confirmed that Chen Dabin was aware of Fukang Company's shareholder composition, assets and liabilities, etc. The three "Overdue Loan Collection Notices" bearing Huaxi Pharmaceutical's seal and the fact that Huaxi Pharmaceutical continued to pay loan interest until December 31, 2004, also confirmed that Huaxi Pharmaceutical ratified the guarantee and actually performed it. (2) Chen Dabin, the legal representative of Huaxi Pharmaceutical, was the actual user and beneficiary of the loan. Fukang Company, Yuanchang Industry, and Agricultural Resources Company had existing old loans with Dazhu Credit Union. Chen Dabin directly participated in the actual operation of Yuanchang Industry, repaying the overdue loan of RMB 4 million. Chen Dabin had significant interests in Yuanchang Industry, Chengdu Dayi Property Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dayi Property), Chengdu Dayi Industry (Group) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dayi Industry), and was also the focus of interests in the merger of Dayi Industry, the borrowing of Fukang Company, and the guarantee of Huaxi Pharmaceutical in this case. Fukang Company repaid the old loans of Yuanchang Industry and Agricultural Resources Company, and it was inevitable that Huaxi Pharmaceutical would become the guarantor for Fukang Company's new loan. After the loan was made, Huaxi Pharmaceutical continued to fulfill the obligation to pay interest on behalf of Fukang Company, rather than the guarantor performing the guarantee obligation only when the borrower failed to repay the loan at maturity, indicating that Fukang Company was not the actual user of this loan. 3. In this case, Fukang Company used its own funds to repay the previous loan and then borrowed a new loan, as evidenced by original accounting vouchers such as bank drafts, credit slips, deposit/withdrawal slips, and transfer vouchers. At the same time, according to the accounting subjects, accounting entries, and text content recorded on the vouchers, the aforementioned vouchers have continuous bookkeeping, unique order, and none of the vouchers can be missing or exchanged. The fund flow is clear and is a typical "repayment first, then loan," rather than "using a new loan to repay an old loan."

This Court is of the opinion that the issues in dispute in this case are: 1. Whether the failure of the second-instance court to list Fukang Company as a defendant in this case constitutes an omission of a party; 2. Whether the admission of evidence by the second-instance court violated legal procedures; 3. Whether the change in the members of the collegiate panel by the second-instance court was duly notified to the parties in accordance with the law; 4. Whether the loan of RMB 12 million involved in this case was actually disbursed; 5. Whether Huaxi Pharmaceutical should bear the guarantee liability.

I. Regarding the issue of whether a party was omitted in this case. Article 4 of the "Guaranteed Loan Contract" signed by Dazhu Credit Union, Fukang Company, and Huaxi Pharmaceutical clearly stipulates: "The loan guarantor, Tibet Huaxi Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd., voluntarily serves as the guarantor for the borrower's timely repayment of the principal and interest of the loan under this contract. The guarantor shall assume joint and several liability for the borrower's acts in breach of contract such as diverting the use of the loan." Accordingly, it should be determined that Huaxi Pharmaceutical is the guarantor assuming joint and several liability for the loan. According to Article 53 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "In a lawsuit arising from a dispute over a guarantee contract... where the creditor only sues the guarantor, unless the guarantee contract clearly stipulates that the guarantor assumes joint and several liability, the people's court shall notify the principal debtor to participate in the lawsuit as a co-defendant; where the creditor only sues the principal debtor, the principal debtor may be listed as the sole defendant." Dazhu Credit Union's filing of this lawsuit only against Huaxi Pharmaceutical as the defendant complies with legal provisions. Although Fukang Company still enjoyed the right to participate in litigation after its business license was revoked on April 26, 2001, since Dazhu Credit Union did not assert its rights against it, the failure of the first-instance and second-instance courts to list Fukang Company as a defendant in this case complies with legal provisions.

II. Regarding the issue of whether the admission of evidence by the second-instance judgment violated legal procedures. First, all evidence submitted by Dazhu Credit Union in the litigation had been cross-examined in multiple court sessions, and most of the evidence was in original form. Although the "Merger Agreement" was a copy, Huaxi Pharmaceutical did not object to it during cross-examination in the first instance of this case, only claiming that the agreement was not performed. Although it later raised an objection in the second instance, it did not provide contrary evidence, and this evidence was not the main evidence for determining the basic facts of this case. Therefore, Huaxi Pharmaceutical's claim that the evidence submitted by Dazhu Credit Union was in copy form and its authenticity could not be confirmed is inconsistent with the facts and does not constitute grounds for retrial in this case.

Second, Article 28 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings provides: "Where a party entrusts a relevant department to make an appraisal conclusion on its own, and the other party has sufficient evidence to rebut it and applies for a new appraisal, the people's court shall permit it." According to this provision, appraisal conclusions made by relevant departments entrusted by a party on its own are not necessarily inadmissible. The Dazhou Jinzheng Judicial Appraisal Center's acceptance of the entrustment by Dazhu Credit Union to produce the Da Jin Si Jian Zhong Xin (2009) Si Jian Zi No. 002 "Judicial Appraisal Opinion Letter" complies with legal provisions. Dazhu Credit Union's submission of this appraisal opinion letter as evidence does not violate legal procedures. This appraisal was made regarding the bank documents involved in this case. Huaxi Pharmaceutical cannot prove that the above documents are false, and its claim that the appraisal conclusion is erroneous also lacks basis.

Third, the four pieces of evidence obtained by the court ex officio to which Huaxi Pharmaceutical objected are: the "Investigation Record" made by the second-instance court regarding Shen Mingcheng, the legal representative of Fukang Company; the "Consultation Record" of the second-instance court's investigation at the Dazhou Banking Regulatory Bureau; the Da Shi Nong Hang (2000) No. 306 document of the Dazhou Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China; and two sets of vouchers for Dazhu Credit Union's loans to other companies during the same period. The trial records of the second instance indicate that the above evidence had been cross-examined, and Huaxi Pharmaceutical submitted a written objection. Regarding the "Investigation Record" formed when Shen Mingcheng did not appear in court, according to Article 69 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, witness testimony from witnesses who did not appear in court cannot be used alone as the basis for determining the facts of the case. In this case, the second-instance court did not use Shen Mingcheng's testimony alone as the basis for determining the facts, but rather used it as corroborating evidence, together with the industrial and commercial registration of Fukang Company, the document of the Dazhou Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, Huaxi Pharmaceutical's statements in the litigation, and the relevant vouchers for the flow of funds involved in the case, to confirm the facts of this case. This was not improper. Because the dispute in this case involves a certain level of professionalism in the banking industry, it was not illegal for the second-instance court to conduct an investigation and consultation at the Dazhou Banking Regulatory Bureau. From the content of the "Consultation Record," the statements of the consulted person were not contradictory, and the consulted person also signed the record to confirm it. The court's investigation and consultation procedure was lawful. The Da Shi Nong Hang (2000) No. 306 document records the basic information of Hainan Company, Fukang Company, and Dayi Industry, among which the content regarding Chen Dabin's capital contribution to Fukang Company and his status as a shareholder of Fukang Company is consistent with the industrial and commercial registration of Fukang Company. This evidence is relevant to this case. The vouchers for Dazhu Credit Union's loans to other companies were submitted to ascertain whether the old loans involved in this case existed, and Huaxi Pharmaceutical also made corresponding claims in the litigation. This evidence is also relevant to this case.

In summary, there is no situation where the second-instance court admitted evidence in violation of legal procedures.

III. Regarding the issue of whether the change in the members of the collegiate panel by the second-instance court was duly notified to the parties in accordance with the law. The trial record of the second instance on March 22, 2010, records that the court notified both parties during the court session that the collegiate panel member Liu Zhidong had been replaced by Chen Hong. This record is signed and confirmed by the agents of both parties. Therefore, Huaxi Pharmaceutical's claim in this application for retrial is inconsistent with the facts.

IV. Regarding the issue of whether Dazhu Credit Union actually disbursed the loan of RMB 12 million. Dazhu Credit Union submitted the "Loan Voucher," "Deposit Slip," "Withdrawal Slip," and "Letter of Entrusted Draft" to prove that on the date of signing the "Guaranteed Loan Contract," Dazhu Credit Union disbursed a loan of RMB 12 million to Fukang Company and transferred it into the deposit account No. 201100181 of Fukang Company at Dazhu Credit Union. Subsequently, Fukang Company transferred the funds by draft through account No. 821000843 opened at the Dazhu County Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China by Dazhu Credit Union. The "Loan Voucher" bears the transfer stamp of Dazhu Credit Union, the company seal of Fukang Company, and the seal of Shen Mingcheng, the legal representative of Fukang Company. The "Withdrawal Slip" also bears the transfer stamp of Dazhu Credit Union and the financial seal of Fukang Company, indicating that the loan was actually disbursed. Moreover, after the loan was disbursed, Huaxi Pharmaceutical and its affiliated companies paid interest to Dazhu Credit Union until December 31, 2004, a period of five years. Dazhu Credit Union sent notices for the recovery of overdue loans to the borrower Fukang Company and the guarantor Huaxi Pharmaceutical on July 23, 1999, October 23, 2000, and November 22, 2002, which were confirmed by Huaxi Pharmaceutical, also corroborating that the loan of RMB 12 million had been disbursed. In the first and second instances before the case was remanded for retrial, Huaxi Pharmaceutical did not object to the actual disbursement of the loan, only claiming that it was a loan used to repay a loan. Therefore, considering the evidence of Dazhu Credit Union's disbursement of the loan, the evidence of Huaxi Pharmaceutical's payment of interest, and Huaxi Pharmaceutical's admission in the litigation, the second-instance court's finding that Dazhu Credit Union had actually disbursed the loan was well-supported by evidence.

V. Regarding the issue of whether Huaxi Pharmaceutical should bear the guarantee liability. First, the "Guaranteed Loan Contract" bears the signatures and seals of Fukang Company, Huaxi Pharmaceutical, and Dazhu Credit Union, and the signatures of their legal representatives. Huaxi Pharmaceutical did not object to the contract in the initial first instance, second instance, and retrial of this case. Although it later claimed that Article 11 of the contract, "If the borrower fails to repay at maturity, the guarantor shall be responsible for repayment and assume joint and several liability," was added, this provision is not inconsistent with Article 4 of the contract, which states that Huaxi Pharmaceutical voluntarily serves as the guarantor for the borrower's timely repayment of the principal and interest of the loan under this contract and assumes joint and several liability for the borrower's acts in breach of contract such as diverting the use of the loan. Therefore, it does not affect the determination that Huaxi Company should assume joint and several guarantee liability.

Second, after the loan was disbursed, Huaxi Pharmaceutical and its affiliated companies paid interest on behalf of Fukang Company until December 31, 2004. During this period, the three notices for the recovery of overdue loans sent by Dazhu Credit Union to Fukang Company and Huaxi Pharmaceutical were all confirmed by Huaxi Pharmaceutical. This should be regarded as a further confirmation of the guarantee liability by Huaxi Company.

Thirdly, the stipulation in Article 4 of the Guaranteed Loan Contract regarding Huaxi Pharmaceutical's assumption of joint and several liability for the borrowing party's acts of transferring the loan purpose and other breaches of this contract does not violate legal provisions. Huaxi Company's commitment to assume joint and several liability even for acts such as Fukang Company's transfer of the loan purpose means it should have foreseen the various guarantee risks arising from Fukang Company's transfer of the loan purpose. Since refinancing of a loan constitutes one form of transferring the loan purpose, even if refinancing existed in this case, because Huaxi Pharmaceutical had made a prior commitment, its assertion that Fukang Company and Dazhu Credit Union maliciously colluded to change the loan purpose is unfounded, and Huaxi Company should still bear guarantee liability under the contract. The business registration materials of Fukang Company are consistent with the contents concerning Fukang Company's shareholders as mentioned in Document No. 306 [2000] of Dazhou Agricultural Bank. As Fukang Company's guarantor, Huaxi Pharmaceutical raised no objection to Fukang Company's business registration materials during the first and second instances of this case, meaning it had no objection to Chen Dabin's status as a shareholder and supervisor of Fukang Company, thereby constituting an admission of this fact. Therefore, the aforementioned evidence corroborates Huaxi Pharmaceutical's admission in the litigation, and it can be established that Chen Dabin was a shareholder holding 50% of Fukang Company's shares and a supervisor of Fukang Company. Whether Chen Dabin's signature in Fukang Company's business registration materials is genuine does not affect the public notice and public trust validity thereof. Consequently, even if refinancing existed in this case, given Chen Dabin's special status as the legal representative of Huaxi Pharmaceutical, supervisor of Fukang Company, and one of its two shareholders, as well as Huaxi Pharmaceutical's and its affiliated companies' actions in repaying the loan interest on behalf of Fukang Company, Huaxi Pharmaceutical should have been aware of the actual purpose of the loan. Therefore, in accordance with Article 39 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, Huaxi Pharmaceutical should still bear the guarantee liability in this case.

In summary, the retrial application of Huaxi Pharmaceutical does not meet the circumstances specified in Article 179, paragraph 1, items (2) and (6) and paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 181, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

The retrial application of Tibet Huaxi Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. is rejected.

Presiding Judge: Chen Yifang

Acting Judge: Liu Xiaofei
